research_mode: official Ministry of Justice and HMPPS accredited custody-safety statistics only; rolling-period, classification, population and sex-estate comparability gates; no parcel, exact-location, candidate or business result claimed

sources.name: Safety-in-custody scope
verified_claims: Safety-in-custody statistics cover deaths, self-harm and assaults in prison custody in England and Wales.
limitations: Prison-custody measures are not indicators of residential parcel safety.

sources.name: Different reporting endpoints
verified_claims: The release covers deaths to March 2026 and assaults and self-harm to December 2025 using rolling 12-month measures.
limitations: Measures with different endpoints must not be compared as if they cover the same period.

sources.name: Accredited custody statistics
verified_claims: The release is labelled accredited official statistics and is produced under UK Statistics Authority-approved arrangements.
limitations: Accreditation does not remove provisional classification or rolling-period limitations.

sources.name: Deaths in prison custody
verified_claims: There were 352 deaths in prison custody in the 12 months to March 2026, 12% fewer than the previous 12 months.
limitations: The prison-estate total must not be converted into community risk.

sources.name: Self-inflicted death count
verified_claims: There were 67 self-inflicted deaths in the 12 months to March 2026, 28% fewer than the previous period.
limitations: Cause classifications can be revised after further evidence or inquests.

sources.name: Awaiting-classification deaths
verified_claims: Of 74 deaths classified as other, 43 were awaiting further information before final classification.
limitations: Category totals are provisional and may be revised upward after inquests or tests.

sources.name: Quarterly death volatility
verified_claims: Quarterly death figures should be interpreted cautiously because of greater volatility and possible seasonal effects.
limitations: A single-quarter movement must not be treated as a stable trend.

sources.name: Population-adjusted interpretation
verified_claims: The publication presents incident rates per 1,000 prisoners because prison-population changes affect raw incident counts.
limitations: Raw counts and rates answer different questions and must remain separate.

sources.name: COVID-period comparability
verified_claims: Comparability between 2020 and 2022 and other periods is affected by prison restrictions introduced during the COVID-19 pandemic.
limitations: Trend comparisons across the restriction period require contextual adjustment.

sources.name: Youth-custody age-mix change
verified_claims: Retention of young people in youth custody until age 19 between November 2022 and November 2024 changed age profiles in youth and adult estates.
limitations: Age-group comparisons across this period are not strictly like for like.

sources.name: Self-harm incident total
verified_claims: There were 72,753 reported self-harm incidents in the 12 months to December 2025, 8% fewer than the previous period.
limitations: Incident totals can be heavily influenced by repeated events involving the same individuals.

sources.name: Self-harm incident rate
verified_claims: The self-harm incident rate was 837 per 1,000 prisoners in the 12 months to December 2025.
limitations: An incident rate can exceed 1,000 because individuals may have multiple incidents.

sources.name: Individuals self-harming
verified_claims: There were 13,394 individuals who self-harmed in the latest 12 months, 3.5% fewer than the prior period.
limitations: Individual counts and incident counts must not be treated as the same denominator.

sources.name: Repeated self-harm concentration
verified_claims: Just over half of prisoners who self-harmed in 2025 did so more than once.
limitations: Incident counts cannot be interpreted as unique-person counts.

sources.name: Female-estate self-harm rate
verified_claims: The self-harm rate in female establishments was over nine times the rate in male establishments.
limitations: Different estate populations and repeated incidents require careful interpretation.

sources.name: Hospital-attendance self-harm
verified_claims: Self-harm incidents requiring hospital attendance decreased by 13% to 3,015.
limitations: Hospital-attendance data measure a subset and not total clinical severity.

sources.name: Total assault rate
verified_claims: There were 31,345 assaults, a rate of 360 per 1,000 prisoners and a 2.7% rate increase.
limitations: Prison assault rates must not be compared directly with community crime rates.

sources.name: Prisoner-on-prisoner assaults
verified_claims: The prisoner-on-prisoner assault rate increased by 6% to 247 per 1,000 prisoners.
limitations: The rate is specific to the custodial estate and reporting definitions.

sources.name: Assaults on staff
verified_claims: The overall staff-assault rate fell by 4.5%, while it increased by 12% in female establishments.
limitations: Overall and estate-specific movements can differ and must not be collapsed into one trend.

sources.name: Serious-assault rate
verified_claims: There were 3,484 serious assaults, a rate of 40 per 1,000 prisoners and a 2.8% increase.
limitations: Serious-assault counts remain custodial-estate statistics and do not provide parcel evidence.
